A US proposal to restore Russian energy supplies to Europe through Ukraine reportedly alarmed Kyiv because it resembled ideas promoted by Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev.
Remembering Adnan Kivan: a Legacy With a Future — A personal tribute to the late owner of Kyiv Post, who transformed the publication into Ukraine’s genuine “global voice.”

Nord Stream Trial Continues as Court Rejects Defence Bid to Halt Proceedings — German prosecutors urged a Hamburg court to reject a defense request to halt the Nord Stream sabotage trial, arguing that Ukrainian military secrecy obligations do not prevent Serhii Kuznetsov from receiving a fair trial. The court had not announced a decision as of publication.

What Israel’s Election Could Change for Ukraine and Relations With Russia — Israelis head to the polls focused on security, living costs, and domestic divisions. Opposition leader Yair Lapid has promised greater support for Ukraine, while Netanyahu’s government has pursued a cautious rapprochement. For Kyiv, the test will be whether those positions produce practical military cooperation.

Russia Observing Ceasefire in Occupied Oleshky as Humanitarian Mission Begins — Russian forces were observing a localized ceasefire around occupied Oleshky in Kherson Oblast as of 9 a.m. on Oct. 27, Ukraine’s Marine Corps said, as a humanitarian mission began in the city amid worsening conditions for civilians.

Moscow to Restrict Mobile Internet for 3 Days During Putin’s Summits — Moscow will restrict mobile internet for three days during the Gas Exporting Countries Forum and Russia-Africa summit, citing security concerns. The shutdowns come amid intensified Ukrainian drone attacks on the Moscow region and follow weeks-long outages in the capital earlier this year.

Ukraine Downs 2 Ballistic Missiles, 255 Russian Drones in Overnight Attack Targeting Kyiv — Ukrainian air defenses shot down or neutralized two ballistic missiles and 255 Russian drones during an overnight attack primarily targeting Kyiv, the Air Force reported. Israel to Give Verdict on Netanyahu in Pivotal Election — Israelis are voting in a closely contested election that could end Netanyahu’s long rule after the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack. Security, accountability for the failures, and Israel’s rightward shift dominate the race, with coalition talks likely to take weeks or months.

Ukraine Asks 5 European Allies for Patriot Missiles — Ukraine has asked the UK, France, Germany, Italy, and Poland to provide 10% of their existing Patriot and IRIS-T interceptor stocks in exchange for future deliveries. Kyiv also seeks MANPADS and funding to double drone production by 2027 as Russia prepares intensified strikes.

The agreement aims to facilitate humanitarian aid and evacuations, but implementation and monitoring arrangements remain unclear.
